Runtime guide

Tokio provides the runtime used by this documentation example. Applications run asynchronous network tasks on a scheduler and reserve blocking threads for synchronous work. The distinction is useful when HTML parsing and network requests share a backend, because parsing should not hold up unrelated requests.

Shared state

Use shared ownership for immutable configuration and short critical sections for counters. Never hold a synchronous lock across a network await. Each operation should have its own timeout and resource budget, so a public server remains responsive when a dependency becomes slow.

Testing

Use deterministic fixtures to exercise extraction independently of the public Internet. Test redirects and forbidden destinations before opening a service to external visitors. Measure concurrency on actual deployment hardware and inspect latency rather than claiming unlimited capacity.
